checks.what: achaemenid-empire gain -515 from nobody, Cliopatria Achaemenid -500 outline intersected with Sistan and Baluchestan (690 of the province's 691 cells, about 174,500 km2). 171 of these cells (Sistan, the Drangiana part) are already Achaemenid. The event moves only the 520 unowned cells, all south of 29.6N (Baluchestan and Makran), so the region covers Gedrosia and no foreign land. The Gedrosia page supports the land and the conqueror: 'It was conquered by Cyrus the Great or Darius the Great'; Gedrosia 'runs from the Indus River to the north-eastern edge of the Strait of Hormuz', south of Arachosia and Drangiana, east of Carmania. The page gives no year. The year -515 bridges to the dossier's Indus event (ledger/13). The Darius the Great page, which I also opened, supports that: 'Darius conquered the lands surrounding the Indus River in 515 BCE', and he sent Scylax 'to explore the Indian Ocean from the mouth of the Indus to Suez'. The year falls in the range the page allows, and the entry is honestly flagged confidence 1. Effect, checked by my own trial: the hole inside the empire is filled 15 years earlier, the -500 snap drops from 1260 to 741 added cells (next-window trial), and nothing else changes.

wu_-584 (-584..-551): Cliopatria Wu -750 (955 cells) minus the Xu heartland. The cut spec is identical to xu/ledger/0, xu_-750 and wu/ledger/2 (96 cells, of which 47 lie inside the Wu shape), so it removes exactly Xu's land. The Xu page supports it: in 584 'Xu was also attacked by Wu forces'; 'Reduced to its heartland, Xu was eventually conquered by Wu in 512 BC.' In the trial the wu/xu R2 conflict (47 cell-years) disappears, Xu keeps 95 cells from -584 to -513, and Wu takes 74 at -512 through wu/ledger/2.

wu_-550: Cliopatria Wu -550 (the same 955 cells as -750) minus the same Xu heartland spec; it keeps the dossier's span (to -481, then wu_-480). Same page sentence as overrides/0. In the trial Xu holds its 95 cells through -513, Wu gains the heartland at -512 and keeps it to the window's end (wu 833 inside its shape at -512 and -501), and the wu_-550 snap no longer touches Xu.

median-kingdom_-600: the dossier's own corrected outline (Median -600 minus Afghanistan and Pakistan, plus the Turkish part of Achaemenid -550), copied verbatim, minus Urartu's -600 keyframe as the urartu dossier corrects it (538 cells, about 136,000 km2, Commagene and the Malatya strip excluded as in that dossier). It cuts exactly Urartu's land. The Urartu page supports it: 'The Medes then took over the Urartian capital of Van in 590 BC, effectively ending the sovereignty of Urartu'; Rusa IV '609-590 or 585 BC'; no earlier date for Median control. In the trial the urartu/median R2 conflict (404 cell-years) is gone and the Median -600 snap drops from 443 to 39 added cells. Urartu holds all 538 cells -600..-591, the Medes take all 538 at -590 (urartu/ledger/11), and the Achaemenids take 535 at -550, as before.

sabaeans_-550: Cliopatria Sabaeans -550 (268 cells) united with Cliopatria Qataban -350 (52 cells, the Wadi Bayhan; the two shapes do not overlap), 320 cells in all. The Qataban page supports it: 'During the 6th century BCE, Qatabān had come under the control of Sabaʾ'; it 'regained its independence in the late 5th century BCE'; 'centred around the Wādī Bayhān'. This matches sabaeans/ledger/7 and qataban/ledger/1 at -550. In the published draft the Qataban land was unowned from -550 to -501; in the trial Saba holds all 52 cells from -550 to -501, and the -550 snap removes 4 cells instead of 56.

sabaeans_-450, a next-window keyframe effective -450..-421 because the dossier's new sabaeans_-420 takes over at -420: Cliopatria Sabaeans -450 plus Qataban -350, with the same page sentences as overrides/3. I ran a trial of m0500-m0401 with this patch in place: Saba holds the 52 Qataban cells through -421, they return to Qataban at -420 (qataban/ledger/2), and the end anchor m0400 is unchanged for them. The entry is consistent with the dossiers' 420 independence. The seam crossing is reported under problems.
